articles.title: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.mainIdea: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term
articles.summary: Argus Research: Technical Assessment: Bullish in the Intermediate-Term. The major indices finished December on the downside and provided very mixed results for the month. The S&P 500, S&P 100, S&P MidCap 400 (MDY), and the Russell 1000 were flat. The Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) and the Russell 2000 (IWM) fell 0.7%, and the S&P SmallCap 600 (SML) dropped 0.3%. Finally, the Dow Industrials rose 0.7% while the NYSE tacked on 0.8%. Financials led the 11 sectors in December, racing ahead by 3.1%. Communication Services popped 2.4%, Materials gained 2%, Industrials added 1.3%, and Consumer Discretionary was up 1.2%. Utilities were clocked, dropping 5.1%, Real Estate lost 2%, and Healthcare and Consumer Staples fell almost 1.4%. Aluminum was the top industry, surging 27%. Nonferrous metals jumped 18%, while Trucking, Broadcasting & Entertainment, and Real Estate Holding rose just over 10%. Home Construction was whacked, falling 10%, while Specialty Retailers declined 9%, Drug Retailers, Recreational Products, and Conventional Electricity all gave up 6% for the month. For all of 2025, the major indices finished their third straight year of outsized gains, with the S&P 500 rising 16.4%, the Nasdaq and Nasdaq 100 popping 20%, the S&P 100 adding 19%, the Dow Jones Industrial and Russell 2000 tacking on 13%, the S&P MidCap 400 climbing 6% and the S&P SmallCap 600 adding 4%. Turning to sectors, Information Technology led again in 2025, up 25%, followed by Communications Services (+23%), Industrials (+19%), Utilities (+16%), and Financials and Healthcare (both +15%). Consumer Staples was up 3.9% and Real Estate 3%. Related tickers mentioned: AAPL, ALI=F, GE, ^DJI, ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^SP400, ^SP600.
